title: Dust, perfect fluids and the Newtonian limit
promptMarkdown:

Continuity and Euler derived with the approximations v ≪ c and P ≪ ρc² stated and interpreted (γ → 1; pressure no longer contributes to inertia).

levels.description: Both equations, both approximations with meaning.

criteria.criterion: ∂_μ(ρu^μ) = 0 obtained by contracting with u_ν; hence ρu^μ∂_μu^ν = 0, i.e. dust particles move on straight lines (the acceleration-free equation that becomes the geodesic equation later).

checkExamples.label: correct solution
checkExamples.text: In the Newtonian limit we take v ≪ c so that γ ≈ 1 and P ≪ ρc² so that pressure does not contribute to inertia. The ν = 0 equation gives ∂_t ρ + ∇·(ρv) = 0 and the ν = j equation, after using continuity, gives ρ(∂_t v + v·∇v) = −∇P, Euler's equation.

checkExamples.label: limit without hypotheses
checkExamples.text: Taking the Newtonian limit of the conservation law gives Euler's equation ρ dv/dt = −∇P.

checkExamples.label: no Euler equation
checkExamples.text: I derived the continuity equation from the ν = 0 component but did not finish the momentum equation.
